findings.detail: The stats line is built inline with four chained conditional segments inside one template literal on a single line. It is the hardest line to read in the new code, and because it lives in the component the only way it gets tested is through a real browser — `e2e/web-scraper-fresha.spec.ts:93` and `:159` assert its wording via `page.getByText(/…/)`, which costs a 90 s Playwright test to verify pure string formatting. Pulling it into the pure module makes the same assertion a one-line vitest case and keeps the component to orchestration.
findings.summary: Fresha success log is a ~450-char template literal with four nested ternaries

findings.detail: The catch branches on `controller.signal.aborted` rather than on which failure actually occurred. Once the 45 s timer has fired, a genuinely different failure — `!res.ok` landing at the same moment, or a parse that returns null on a slow large page — is rewritten as `The venue page did not answer within 45 s.` The user impact is nil today (the component discards this message and logs its own generic fallback text at WebScraperTab.tsx:211, so the precise wording only reaches `console.warn`), which is why this is low and not medium. It would become a real diagnosis problem the moment the FreshaVenueError message is surfaced to the user or to a log sink.
findings.summary: Any error thrown after the deadline is reported as a timeout

findings.detail: `handbooks/architecture/frontend-boundaries.md` § rule 2 flags a literal `fetch(` under `components/`, and `(u, init) => fetch(u, init)` matches that pattern textually. Recording explicitly that I do not consider this a violation: the request, headers, abort timer and error shaping all live in `services/freshaVenueService.ts`; the component only supplies the browser primitive through the service's `FetchTextLike` parameter. That seam is exactly what lets `tests/unit/freshaVenue.test.ts:283-305` exercise the service with no network, which is the outcome rule 2 exists to protect. It is also the established convention in this file — the pre-existing Yalla path at line 63 is identical. No change requested; noted so a future rule-match on this line is not re-litigated.
findings.summary: Checked and cleared: the literal `fetch` in the component is a DI seam, not I/O
